summary.text: 动 means ‘act’ or ‘move’ and is the simplified form of 動. In traditional 動, 力 contributes meaning, while 重 is proposed as a sound cue because its ‘heavy’ reading was similar to 動 in Old Chinese. The reconstruction comparison has not been independently verified in the recorded research.

formation.text: The received traditional form 動 is phonosemantic: 力 contributes meaning associated with strength or action, and 重 supplies a proposed sound cue. This analysis does not establish that these same parts were present in the reported bronze-script graph.

components.text: In the received form 動, 力 contributes meaning associated with strength or action. Its presence as a separate component in the reported bronze-script graph is uncertain.

In the received form 動, 重 is the phonetic component. The proposed comparison uses its ‘heavy’ reading; early forms of 重 have been interpreted as a person bearing a load, but the object’s name and pronunciation are not established.

sound_limitation.text: The comparison concerns 動 and 重 in its ‘heavy’ reading. It does not establish the name or pronunciation of the object interpreted as a load in early forms of 重.

sound.text: In the Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstructions, 動 *[Cə-ә m-]tˤoŋʔ and 重 *N-t<r>oŋʔ in its ‘heavy’ reading are similar enough to support a proposed phonetic relationship. The same system gives 重 ‘repeat’ a distinct reconstruction. The comparison was not independently verified in the recorded research.

history.text: A paleographic account identifies a bronze-script graph catalogued as 童 with 動. The selected bronze-style rendering shows this candidate graph. Its original referent and identification remain uncertain, and no direct sequence linking it to the received form is established.

The received form’s analysis as 力 plus phonetic 重 is transmitted in the seal-script tradition. The selected seal-style rendering illustrates this analysis, without establishing a direct transition from the bronze-style graph.
The 1956 scheme standardized 动 as the simplified form paired with 動. The history of the cloud-like portion’s shape is unresolved.
An old form 𨔝 is recorded with 辵. No graphic sequence connecting that form to 动 is established.

uncertainties.text: No oracle-bone form or absolute date for the earliest graph is given. The reported bronze-script identification, the graph’s referent, and its connection to the received form remain uncertain.
Early forms of 重 have been interpreted as a person bearing a bag or load, but the object’s identity and spoken name are not established. This does not determine 重’s phonetic role in received 動.

senses.text: The transmitted gloss 作也 means ‘act’ or ‘do.’ Cited textual and manuscript examples also show action or movement, but are not dated precisely enough here to order them.
A cited Mawangdui manuscript example uses 動 for changing position or state. Its development in relation to the action sense is unresolved.
Modern records include ‘move’ and ‘happen,’ as well as the nouns ‘movement’ and ‘action.’ The evidence does not establish a single chronological path among these meanings.

developments.text: Both uses are attested, but their transition and direction are unresolved.

limitations.text: The cited textual and manuscript passages do not provide absolute dates sufficient to establish the chronology of these senses.
The early bronze graph’s meaning and its semantic path to ‘act’ or ‘move’ remain unresolved.

overview.text: 动 means ‘act’ or ‘move’ and is the simplified form of 動. In traditional 動, 力 contributes meaning, and 重 is proposed as a sound cue because its ‘heavy’ reading was similar to 動 in Old Chinese; the reconstruction comparison has not been independently verified.

components.text: In traditional 動, 力 links the character with strength or action.
In traditional 動, 重 is proposed as a sound cue through its ‘heavy’ reading. The proposed comparison does not establish the name or pronunciation of the load interpreted in early forms of 重.

relationships.text: 力 contributes meaning in the received traditional form 動.
重 is the reported phonetic component in traditional 動. The proposed comparison uses 重’s ‘heavy’ reading but could not be independently verified in the recorded research.
The 1956 scheme paired 动 with 動 as its simplified form.
